messages.subject: Re: combining ImzMLs in Cardinal
messages.body_plain:
You can use the aptly-named combine method for this. For example:

# generate some test data
msset1 <- generateImage(data=diag(2), as="MSImageSet")
sampleNames(msset1) <- "A"
msset2 <- generateImage(data=diag(2), as="MSImageSet")
sampleNames(msset2) <- "B"

# combine the datasets
msset3 <- combine(msset1, msset2)

# plot sample 'A'
image(msset3, mz=1, subset=sample %in% "A")

# plot both samples
image(msset3, mz=1, layout=c(1,2))

If you read the data from imzML files, the sample names should already be uniquely generated from the file names.

To combine datasets, the m/z values need to match up, so if you get an error and the sample names are different, that is the most likely culprit.

Make sure the m/z values are the same for both datasets.

You can use the reduceDimension method to resample or bin the mass spectra to a common set of m/z values before combining the datasets if necessary. Or simple re-assign using mz<- if they should be the same but are off by a rounding error.

Hope this helps!

Kyle

messages.subject: Re: Issue installing Cardinal in R
messages.body_plain:
Hi Catie,

Cardinal is currently only available on the development version of Bioconductor, which requires the development version of R. If you install the development version of R from CRAN (scroll down to "other builds" on the download page), and then follow the Bioconductor installation instructions, it should work.

Cardinal will be included in the next public release of Bioconductor on April 17, at which point it will be installable from an ordinary installation of R.

Rtools includes the tools for developing R packages on Windows, and is only necessary if you are building and installing the package from source. It's not necessary if you are installing from Bioconductor.

I hope this helps.

Kyle

messages.subject: Re: Issue installing Cardinal in R
messages.body_plain:
It looks like this is due to R 3.2 and Bioconductor 3.1 are both getting ready for release. Bioconductor is expecting R version 3.2, while the development branch of R has moved on to version 3.3.

You can download the test version of R 3.2 for Windows here: http://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/rtest.html

I apologize for the confusion. This should all be fixed and working again next month when Bioconductor 3.1 is released.

Kyle
